title: Resistance Mine Attack on Military Column Near Thayetchaung Sparks Indiscriminate Junta Fire, Kills Civilian
detail: Resistance forces mined a military column entering Thayetchaung Township, Tanintharyi Region, in the early morning of September 8, 2026. In response, junta troops fired artillery, small arms and drones indiscriminately into the surrounding area; a 59-year-old woman, Daw Yin Myint of Thayet Hnit Khwa village, was struck and later died from blood loss.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 8 mine attack and junta retaliatory fire near Thayetchaung.

title: KNU Captures Tatmadaw's Htaw Mu Ple Meh Camp in Papun District After 16-Month Siege
detail: The Karen National Union says its forces have taken full control of the military's Htaw Mu Ple Meh camp (also known as Ler Mu Plaw) in Papun (Mutraw) District, Karen State, under the Myanmar military's Southern Command based in Taungoo, Bago Region. A KNU Brigade 5 spokesperson confirmed the camp had been cleared and occupied. KNU forces cut off the camp's ground reinforcement and supply routes starting in May 2025 and maintained a prolonged siege; after months of pressure, military troops abandoned the position and fled on the morning of September 8, 2026, allowing KNU/KNLA forces to enter unopposed.

media.caption: KNU forces take control of the Tatmadaw's Htaw Mu Ple Meh camp in Papun District after a 16-month siege.

title: Blast at MNDAA Explosives Storage Facility in Hsenwi Kills or Wounds at Least 15, Including Chinese Nationals
detail: An explosion tore through an explosives storage facility operated by the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) in Man Mai village, Hsenwi Township, northern Shan State, on September 8, 2026. At least 15 people were killed or injured, including two Chinese nationals, five workers and eight MNDAA members, according to Hsenwi residents. The blast occurred inside the MNDAA compound; Hsenwi has been under MNDAA control since it was seized on January 7, 2024 during Operation 1027. The cause of the explosion was not immediately confirmed.

media.caption: Aftermath of the explosion at an MNDAA explosives storage facility in Man Mai village, Hsenwi Township.
